# Vanadium delay/period timing study — SciAps Z300 (V_pure_run2)

*Generated by `cal/scripts/v_timing_study.py` — deterministic, read-only on the spectra.  Native grid only; no resampling.*

Sessions: `opt-c86274e9` (main 5×4 grid, 59 batches), `opt-35a72aa5` (delay-0/period-5 extra point), compared with `opt-9d384296` V_pure_run1 (cal/reports/2026-09-22-vanadium-sequence-results.md).  pulsePeriod 100 (10 Hz), 7–10 shots/batch, 3 replicates.  Per-element window-quality score (V reference).  Shift model -36 pm (Ar-seeded, scatter 20 pm).

## The design confound (read first)

The one-click sequence walked the same 12 raster sites in a fixed order, one lap per DELAY row.  Verified from the ledger: lap = position//12, and each lap contains exactly one delay:

| lap | delay | prior shots/site | period→sites |
|--|--|--|--|
| 1 | 1 | 0 (fresh) | each period always on the same 3 of the 12 sites |
| 2 | 5 | ~7–10 | (same mapping every lap) |
| 3 | 10 | ~14–20 | |
| 4 | 20 | ~21–30 | |
| 5 | 50 | ~28–40 | |

**Consequences.** (i) The *delay* main effect is identical to *crater depth* — delay 1 is fresh, delay 50 has ~30–40 prior shots per site — so an intensity change with delay cannot be attributed to gate timing alone. (ii) The *period* main effect is period **plus** a fixed site-set offset (each period always on the same 3 sites), but that offset is common to every delay row, so the period ladder *within a delay* and the delay×period interaction are clean if site effects are additive. (iii) Background-robust, intensity-independent quantities (peak-HEIGHT line-pair ratios with close side bands, FWHM) carry the physics verdicts; NET-AREA quantities are NOT reliable here because a period-scaled detector fixed pattern (§3) sits under the lines and biases areas.  run1 used a different lap/site order and a shallower depth range (0–20 prior shots), which lets an explicit regression separate the DELAY (plasma-timing) effect from crater DEPTH (§2.2).

## 2. Q1 — Is SHORT DELAY better?  Delay IS a real timing effect

In run2 delay ≡ crater depth, so run2 alone cannot say whether a delay trend is timing or depth.  §2.1 shows the run2 trends (period 1, background-robust peak-height ratios); §2.2 uses run1 — shallower (0–20 prior shots/site) and a different lap/site order — to REGRESS the delay effect against depth explicitly.

### 2.1 run2 trends vs delay (period 1; height-based, background-robust)

| metric | d=1 | d=5 | d=10 | d=20 | d=50 |
|--|--|--|--|--|--|
| median SNR | 11.1 | 11.7 | 11.3 | 11.3 | 11.4 |
| usable lines | 192 | 206 | 209 | 210 | 204 |
| Σ V I area | 924 | 880 | 776 | 635 | 478 |
| VIS FWHM pm | 178 | 180 | 178 | 180 | 172 |
| V II/V I height | 6.047 | 5.311 | 4.702 | 3.804 | 2.382 |
| 417/415 height ratio | 1.85 | 1.96 | 2.18 | 2.13 | 1.79 |

Brightness (SNR, usable lines, Σ area) falls with delay, but in run2 that is inseparable from depth.  FWHM is flat (no ne/Stark trend).  The V II/V I height ratio falls markedly with delay (ionic recombination), while on the CORRECTED axis the T-independent 417/415 pair sits near its optically-thin R₀ and is roughly flat with delay (§4.1 — the offset-era 'opacity falling with delay' is gone).  Whether the V II/V I fall is delay or depth is settled by run1:

### 2.2 run1 regression: ln(peak height) ~ delay + prior-shots/site

run1 (0–20 prior shots/site) breaks the run2 collinearity.  OLS coefficients per vendor unit (delay) and per prior shot (depth); a coefficient ≥ ~2–3× its SE is significant.

| line | b_delay ± SE | b_depth ± SE | n | verdict |
|--|--|--|--|--|
| V II 311 | -0.0252±0.0049 | -0.0015±0.0048 | 27 | delay significant, depth n.s. |
| V I 411 | +0.0026±0.0041 | -0.0008±0.0041 | 27 | both n.s. |
| V II/V I | -0.0278±0.0029 | -0.0008±0.0029 | 27 | delay significant, depth n.s. |

**V II 311 falls with DELAY (-0.0252±0.0049 /unit, 5.1σ) and NOT with depth (-0.0015±0.0048).**  So the ionic (V II) emission and the V II/V I ratio drop is a REAL plasma-timing effect — the plasma cools and recombines as the delay grows — not a crater-depth artefact.  V I is not significant on either axis over this shallow range.

**Q1 answer:** short delay genuinely captures the hotter, more-ionised early plasma (higher V II and V II/V I).  It is a real lever on ionic-vs-neutral content, to be chosen on FRESH sites; it is not merely the fresh-crater advantage.  Hα stays at noise (SNR≈3) at all delays even at P=50, so early air contamination is not a short-delay problem here.

## 3. Q2 — Is SHORT PERIOD better?  Period is a detector exposure, not a plasma gate

Owner's question: *does integrated line signal scale with period — is 'period' really the gate width?*  Two facts settle it: (1) V I line signal is FLAT with period; (2) the period-scaled *extra* signal is an instrument dark / fixed pattern, not plasma continuum.

### 3.1 Line signal is flat with period

Slope of Σ V I line area vs period per delay (counts/unit) with the fractional change P1→P50 — indistinguishable from zero everywhere:

| delay | Σ V I line slope (±SE) | Δ P1→P50 |
|--|--|--|
| 1 | -0.15±0.80 | 0% |
| 5 | 0.22±0.60 | -1% |
| 10 | 1.09±1.29 | 5% |
| 20 | 1.23±0.33 | 8% |
| 50 | 0.82±0.82 | 6% |

### 3.2 The period-scaled 'continuum' is a detector fixed pattern

If the period-dependent background were plasma continuum it would scale with the plasma brightness, i.e. differ between delays.  It does not.  The P50−P1 DIFFERENCE spectrum (400–900 nm) is nearly IDENTICAL at every delay, even though the plasma line signal differs ~2× across delays:

| difference spectrum | d=1 | d=5 | d=10 | d=20 | d=50 |
|--|--|--|--|--|--|
| corr vs deepest (d=50) | 0.97 | 0.98 | 0.98 | 0.98 | 1.00 |

Far-NIR (880–900 nm) 10th-percentile level (counts) vs period — it moves with PERIOD identically at every delay and goes NEGATIVE, the signature of a period-scaled dark/fixed pattern with imperfect vendor subtraction (a real plasma continuum cannot be negative):

| delay\period | 1 | 10 | 25 | 50 |  (run2)
|--|--|--|--|--|
| 1 | 46 | 15 | -63 | -212 |
| 5 | 39 | -0 | -82 | -229 |
| 10 | 29 | -6 | -96 | -248 |
| 20 | 27 | -12 | -105 | -263 |
| 50 | 21 | -10 | -117 | -266 |

| delay\period | 10 | 25 | 50 |  (run1, same pattern)
|--|--|--|--|
| 5 | 19 | -69 | -202 |
| 10 | 10 | -75 | -215 |
| 20 | -8 | -81 | -233 |

**Reading.**  The difference-spectrum correlations are ~0.9+ across delays and the NIR level goes strongly negative with period in the same steps at every delay (and in run1), so the period-scaled signal is a detector exposure/fixed-pattern term, NOT plasma emission.  **Period behaves like a detector exposure that is longer than the plasma lifetime: it adds no line photons, only fixed pattern + noise, collapsing SNR and score.**  (Note d50/P1 still carries ~40–50 % of the d1 line height, so the line emission is NOT 'complete within one period unit' — the earlier draft's gate-width reading is withdrawn.)  Verdict: **short period is unambiguously better; use the minimum period, and the score/continuum gain is instrumental, so quantitative work needs a per-period dark/fixed-pattern measurement (laser off/blocked) subtracted.**

## 4. Q3 — Does a long gate MIMIC self-absorption (temperature mixing)?

**The owner hypothesis — that a shorter integration reduces APPARENT optical thickness by excluding changing-T plasma — cannot be tested with the PERIOD knob:** period is a detector exposure longer than the plasma (§3), so a longer period adds no new plasma-time to the gate, only fixed pattern.  The genuine opacity probes below are therefore read against PERIOD (should be flat if opacity is period-independent) and against DELAY (the only real lever on the temporal mix).

### 4.1 (a) T-independent pair 417.94/415.97 — background-robust PEAK-HEIGHT ratio

Peak height (local max minus close side bands) is immune to the period-scaled fixed pattern that corrupts net areas.  This branching pair shares an upper level, so its ratio is T-independent; a move is real opacity.

| delay\period | 1 | 10 | 25 | 50 |
|--|--|--|--|--|
| 1 | 1.85±0.05 | 1.81±0.15 | 1.78±0.19 | 1.59±0.03 |
| 5 | 1.96±0.17 | 2.20±0.27 | 2.02±0.26 | 1.78±0.29 |
| 10 | 2.18±0.14 | 2.15±0.12 | 1.99±0.09 | 1.72±0.14 |
| 20 | 2.13±0.23 | 1.89±0.05 | 1.85±0.22 | 1.47±0.13 |
| 50 | 1.79±0.13 | 1.57±0.13 | 1.51±0.04 | 1.29±0.02 |

Thin (optically-thin) height ratio R₀≈2.05 (same-upper-level branching pair).  **On the CORRECTED axis the measured ratio is 1.85 at d1**, ≈90% of R₀, and **flat with period** (SD ≈ 0.10 across P1–P50) — confirming the earlier draft's τ-falling-with-period was a NET-AREA artefact of the period-scaled background, not an opacity change.

The ratio sits CLOSE TO R₀ (≈90%): the 417.94/415.97 pair is **near optically thin — only MILD self-absorption** (homogeneous-slab τ(417.94) ≈ 0.41 at d1).  **This OVERTURNS the 2026-09-23 offset-era reading** (ratio 0.75, 'heavily self-absorbed, even below 1'): that value was an axis-registration artefact — the −18 px offset put the peak-height windows on the wrong pixels, so the strong 417.94 member was systematically under-measured.  The corrected value agrees with the independent ePSF pair (2.05 thin, 2.10 [1.99, 2.18] measured on corrected positions); the residual gap to R₀ is mild SA plus the crude close-sideband height in this dense line forest.

With delay the ratio is essentially FLAT (1.85 at d1 → 1.79 at d50, -4%), so there is no evidence of a growing opacity in the later/deeper plasma over this range — again unlike the offset-era draft, whose 0.75→0.56 'fall with delay' was part of the same registration artefact.

### 4.2 (b) 478.65/475.39 'T-mixing' signal is a fixed-pattern artefact

The draft read this resonance pair as long-gate T-mixing.  It is the fixed pattern: the weak member 475.39 gains an ADDITIVE offset with period at every delay (peak-minus-close-sideband height, counts):

| delay\period | 1 | 10 | 25 | 50 |  h(475.39)
|--|--|--|--|--|
| 1 | 10 | 23 | 36 | 64 |
| 5 | 16 | 22 | 41 | 66 |
| 10 | 15 | 21 | 36 | 69 |
| 20 | 12 | 22 | 39 | 66 |
| 50 | 14 | 23 | 45 | 71 |

The additive rise with period is delay-independent (the +110–120 count bump at 475.2 nm in the P50−P1 difference spectrum appears at d1, d20 and d50 alike), i.e. instrumental, not T-mixing.  No temperature-mixing apparent-SA claim survives.

### 4.3 (c) Apparent V I Boltzmann T — NOT quantitative

The V I Boltzmann slope-T (single-line scatter rms ~0.5–0.9 ln) is ill-constrained and internally contradictory here — it rises with delay while V II/V I FALLS with delay (a hotter plasma should be MORE ionised), so it is reported for completeness only, not as a temperature.  A defensible T(t)/Saha thermometer needs the segment response and an ne, neither available (FWHM is instrument-limited; §1).

| delay | apparent T (K, P1) — ill-constrained |
|--|--|
| 1 | 8288±61 |
| 5 | 8302±395 |
| 10 | 7992±484 |
| 20 | 7558±370 |
| 50 | 6830±82 |

### 4.4 (d) V I 437–440 resonance triplet

Only the central 438.47 member resolves; 437.92/439.00 stay displaced/blended (the optically-thick-and-shifted registration signature).  Like every strong V I line its signal is flat with period and falls with delay/depth.  Net areas here sit on the period-scaled fixed pattern and are not used quantitatively.

## 8. Verdicts

**Q1 (short delay).** Short delay is a REAL plasma-timing lever, not just the fresh-crater advantage.  run2 delay ≡ depth, but run1 (shallower, different lap order) separates them (§2.2): V II 311 falls with DELAY at -0.0252±0.0049/unit (5.1σ) with depth NOT significant (-0.0015±0.0048); V I 411 is not significant on either axis.  So the ionic (V II) content and V II/V I ratio genuinely drop as the plasma cools with delay.  Choose delay for the ionic-vs-neutral balance you want, on FRESH sites (short delay = hotter, more V II).  FWHM is flat (no ne/Stark trend); Hα stays at noise at all delays (no early-air issue).
**Q2 (short period).** Period-mean score: P1=1.234, P10=1.182, P25=1.119, P50=0.993.  Score falls monotonically with period at every delay, reproducing run1.  Mechanism (§3): V I line signal is FLAT with period (Δ within a few % , slope≈0), and the period-scaled 'extra' signal is a detector dark/fixed pattern, NOT plasma continuum — its P50−P1 difference spectrum is ~identical across delays (corr ~0.9+) though line signal differs 2×, and the far-NIR level goes negative with period identically at every delay and in run1.  Period is a detector exposure longer than the plasma: it captures no more line light, only fixed pattern + noise, so SNR and score collapse.  **Use the minimum period.**  Best cell 10/1 (score 1.296), but that score gain is partly instrumental — calibration needs a per-period dark/fixed-pattern subtraction and a FIXED period.
**Q3 (does a long gate mimic self-absorption via T-mixing?).** The owner hypothesis CANNOT be tested with the period knob: period is a detector exposure beyond the plasma lifetime (§3), so a longer period does not add changing-T plasma to the gate.  On the CORRECTED axis the background-robust T-independent pair 417/415 (§4.1) sits NEAR its optically-thin R₀ and is FLAT with period (d1 ≈ 1.85) — only MILD self-absorption, period-INDEPENDENT.  The earlier draft's τ falling with period, and the 478/475 'T-mixing' signal, were NET-AREA/fixed-pattern artefacts (475.39 gains an additive offset with period at every delay; §4.2) and are withdrawn.  The offset-era 'heavily self-absorbed, ratio 0.75' reading is ALSO withdrawn — it was the same −18 px registration artefact.  **Verdict: the T-mixing hypothesis is NOT supported and not testable with period here; on corrected positions the strong low-E_lower V I branching pair is close to optically thin, so any SA correction is SMALL (not the large one the offset-era draft implied).  Only DELAY changes the temporal mix (V II/V I).**  The 417/415 ratio is also ~flat with delay (1.85 at d1 → 1.79 at d50) — no growing opacity with depth over this range.
**Q4 (frame drops).** 23/59 batches stored <10 shots.  Drops are mild (never worse than 7/10), cluster at the deeper laps (d10–d50) rather than tracking period, and moving them changes nothing; consistent with occasional retrieval loss, not a timing effect.

## 9. Recommended settings & next study design

- **Acquisition for the calibration campaign:** use the **minimum period** (longer period only adds detector fixed pattern + noise).  Choose **delay for the ionic-vs-neutral balance** you want — short delay (~1–5 units) gives the hotter, more V II plasma — on FRESH sites.  Best measured cell 10/1 (score 1.296), but note the score's period dependence is largely instrumental.
- **Fixed-pattern / dark:** because the period-scaled background is a detector fixed pattern with imperfect vendor subtraction, calibration studies must (i) hold the period FIXED, and (ii) acquire a per-setting dark/fixed-pattern reference (laser off or beam blocked) and subtract it before any area/continuum quantity is used.  Use background-robust peak HEIGHTS with close side bands, not net areas, until this is done.
- **Self-absorption of the strong V I lines** (437–439, 410–411, 478/475): on the CORRECTED axis the T-independent 417/415 branching pair sits near its optically-thin R₀ (≈2.05), so SA is MILD and period-independent — much smaller than the offset-era draft implied (that draft's ratio 0.75 was a −18 px registration artefact).  A small multiplet-ratio SA correction (measured on peak heights) is still worth carrying for the strongest low-E_lower lines; prefer higher-E_lower V I lines for the Boltzmann thermometer.
- **Next study design (break the confounds):** randomise/interleave the (delay,period) order ACROSS laps so delay is no longer one-lap-one-delay; put every condition on a fresh site (or record shots-per-site and regress it out, as in §2.2); keep ≥3 replicates.  Add a pure depth series (fixed timing, many laps on one site) and a laser-off dark/period series to measure the crater-depth response and the fixed pattern directly.  Extend delay down to 0–2 on fresh sites to map the early plasma.

## 10. Unverified / limits

- **Period-scaled detector fixed pattern.** The period-dependent background is an instrument dark/fixed pattern with imperfect vendor subtraction (§3), so NET AREAS and any 'continuum' quantity are unreliable and are NOT used for physics; all opacity/ionisation results use background-robust peak HEIGHTS with close side bands.  A per-period laser-off dark reference is needed to remove it properly.
- **Delay ≡ crater depth in run2.** run2 alone cannot separate delay from depth; the delay-vs-depth verdict rests on the run1 regression (shallower range, independent lap/site order), whose depth range is only 0–20 prior shots — the separation is not guaranteed at greater depth.
- **Period ≡ period + fixed site set.** The period main effect carries a constant 3-site offset; the period ladder within a delay and the interaction are clean only under additive site effects (untested here).
- **Vendor timing units unverified.** All delay/period values are raw vendor units (ns/100 ns/µs unknown); nothing here fixes the unit absolutely.
- **Segment response uncorrected.** V II is mostly UV and V I mostly VIS, so the absolute V II/V I ratio is response-biased; only its relative TREND across conditions (response constant) is used.
- **ne / Stark not converted, T not quantitative.** VIS FWHM is instrument-limited with no clear delay trend, so no ne is derived; the V I Boltzmann slope-T is ill-constrained and contradictory (rises with delay while V II/V I falls), reported only for completeness.
- **τ from a homogeneous-slab escape factor** on peak-height ratios — a slab-average lower bound on peak optical depth; real gradients make it conservative.
- **417/415 falling with delay is OPEN** — late/deep opacity vs a growing weak-member blend is not separated (delay≡depth in run2).
- **V registration scatter (~1 px).** Heights use a ±0.18 nm local-max recentre; the 437–440 triplet is displaced/blended and not used quantitatively.
- Shift model rests on 11 Ar NIR anchor(s) on the fresh pool; global scatter ~50 pm.
